## Findings
- claim-1: For \(v_{r,s,t,n}\), \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\), \(t>r+s-n\), and \(i=s-t+1,\ j=r-t+1,\ a=\min(n-r-i,r-j),\ b=\min(i,j)\); a valid \((n,r,i,j,a,b,N)\) has all coordinates positive and satisfies \(r<n,\ a+j\le r,\ a+i\le n-r,\ b\le i,j,\ N\le ab\). [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 187-235]
- claim-2: The original and parameter-conjugated cores and both upper shapes satisfy all stated partition, containment, ambient-box, positivity, and valid-tuple conditions; the \(a=0\) boundary has singleton families and admits no valid \(N\).
## Strategy
Let \(q=n-r\). From \(1\le t\le r,s\le n\) and \(t>r+s-n\), one has \(r,s<n\): if \(r=n\), then \(t>s\), contradicting \(t\le s\); similarly for \(s=n\). Put
\[
(r^\vee,s^\vee,t^\vee)=(q,n-s,q-s+t).
\]
Then \(1\le t^\vee\le q,n-s\) and
\[
t^\vee-(q+n-s-n)=t>0,
\]
so this is a bigrassmannian tuple. Its parameters are
\[
i^\vee=j,\quad j^\vee=i,\quad a^\vee=a,\quad b^\vee=b,
\]
since
\[
q-i=t^\vee-1\ge0,\qquad r-j=t-1\ge0,\qquad
a=\min(q-i,r-j),\quad b=\min(i,j).
\]
Hence
\[
i\le q,\ j\le r,\ i+a\le q,\ j+a\le r,\ b\le i,j. \tag{*}
\]

For \(a\ge1\), the requested shape certificate is:

\[
\begin{array}{c|c|c|c|c|c}
\text{ambient}&\text{shape}&\text{width}&\text{height}&
\text{partition and core containment}&\text{box inequalities}\\ \hline
q^r&i^j&i&j&i,j\ge1;\ i^j\subseteq i^j&i\le q,\ j\le r\\
q^r&(i^j,b^a)&i&j+a&
i\ge b;\ i^j\subseteq(i^j,b^a)&i\le q,\ j+a\le r\\
q^r&((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})&i+a&j&
b\le j,\ i+a\ge i;\ i^j\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})
&i+a\le q,\ j\le r\\ \hline
r^q&j^i&j&i&j,i\ge1;\ j^i\subseteq j^i&j\le r,\ i\le q\\
r^q&(j^i,b^a)&j&i+a&
j\ge b;\ j^i\subseteq(j^i,b^a)&j\le r,\ i+a\le q\\
r^q&((j+a)^b,j^{i-b})&j+a&i&
b\le i,\ j+a\ge j;\ j^i\subseteq((j+a)^b,j^{i-b})
&j+a\le r,\ i\le q
\end{array}
\]
All stated box inequalities follow from \((*)\). Thus every partition in each corresponding core-to-upper-shape interval lies in its ambient box.

The two explicit conjugation correspondences are
\[
\{\lambda:i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq(i^j,b^a)\}'
=
\{\mu:j^i\subseteq\mu\subseteq((j+a)^b,j^{i-b})\},
\]
\[
\{\lambda:i^j\subseteq\lambda\subseteq((i+a)^b,i^{j-b})\}'
=
\{\mu:j^i\subseteq\mu\subseteq(j^i,b^a)\}.
\]
They follow by transposing the displayed endpoint partitions.

For \(1\le N\le ab\), both tuples are valid in the source definition [doi:10.1112/jlms.12832, lines 300-304]:

\[
(n,r,i,j,a,b,N):
\quad n,r,i,j,a,b,N\ge1,\quad r<n,
\]
\[
a+j\le r,\quad a+i\le q=n-r,\quad b\le i,j,\quad 1\le N\le ab.
\]

\[
(n,q,j,i,a,b,N):
\quad n,q,j,i,a,b,N\ge1,\quad q<n,
\]
\[
a+i\le q,\quad a+j\le r=n-q,\quad b\le j,i,\quad 1\le N\le ab.
\]
Here \(r,q>0\), \(i,j>0\), \(b>0\), and \(a,N>0\) are explicit; the containment inequalities are those in \((*)\).

Separately, if \(a=0\), then
\[
a=0\iff q-i=0\ \text{or}\ r-j=0
\iff i=q\ \text{or}\ j=r.
\]
Every upper shape equals its core:
\[
(i^j,b^0)=((i+0)^b,i^{j-b})=i^j,
\]
\[
(j^i,b^0)=((j+0)^b,j^{i-b})=j^i.
\]
Thus all four intervals are singleton cores. No valid \(N\) exists, since validity requires \(a\ge1\), equivalently \(1\le N\le ab=0\) is impossible.

This establishes only the requested admissibility certificate.
